NATIONAL

FOREWORD

This Indian Standard (Part 5/See 26) which is identical with ISO 527-5 : 1997 `Plastics -- plastic Determination of tensile properties -- Part 5: Test conditions for unidirectional fibre-reinforced composites' issued by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on the recommendations of the Plastics Sectional Committee and approval of the Petroleum, Coal and Related Products Division Council. The text of ISO Standard has been proposed to be approved as suitable for publication as an Indian Standard without $eviations. Certain conventions are, however, not identical to those used in Indian Standards. Attention is particularly drawn to the following: a) b) Wherever the words `1nternational as `Indian Standard'. Standard' appear referring to this standard, they stmukf be read

Comma (,) has been used as a decimal marker, while in Indian Standards, the current practice is to use a point (.) as the decimal marker.

5

Apparatus

See ISO 527-1, clause 5, except for the following: The micrometer or its equivalent (see 5.2.1) shall read to 0,01 mm or better. It shall have a suitable-size anvil if used on irregular surfaces anda flat anvil if used on flat, smooth (e.g. machined) surfaces. Subclause 5.2.2 does not apply. ball-ended

Care shall be exercised to ensure that the pressure exerted by the grips (see 5.1.3) is only sufficient to prevent the specimen slipping in the grip when loaded to failure. Excessive grip pressure may cause crushing of the specimen due to the low transverse strength of these materials. Hydraulic grips which can be set at a constant grip pressure are preferred. If strain gauges bonded, to the specimen are used, the errors produced by the transverse effect on the transverse gauge will generally be much larger for anisotropic composites than for metals, which are isotropic. Accurate measurement of Poisson's ratio requires correction for this effect. NOTE -- It is recommended that alignment of the specimen and loadingtrain be checked as described in annex B.

Test specimens
Shape and dimensions
on the direction of test relative

Two types of test specimen are specified for use with this part of ISO 527, depending to the fibre direction, as detailed and illustrated in figure 3. 6.1.1 Type A specimen (for longitudinal direction)

Type A specimens shall have a width of 15 mm f 0,5 mm, an overall length of 250 mm and a thickness 1 mm+ 0,2 mm. The sides of each individual specimen shall be parallel to within 0,2 mm. 6.1.2 Type B specimen (for transverse direction)

of

Type B specimens shall have a width of 25 mm A 0,5 mm, an -overall length of 250 mm and a thickness 2 mm* 0,2 mm. The"sides of each individual specimen shall be parallel to within 0,2 mm. For type B specimens 200 mm is acceptable.

6.2.1

Preparation
General

of specimens

In the case of moulding and lamination materials, prepare a panel in accordance with ISO 1286 or another specified/agreed procedure. Cut individual specimens, or groups of specimens (see annex A), from the test panel. In the case of finished products (for example, for quality control during manufacture from flat areas. Take all specimens Parameters annex A. 6.2.2 with their axis within 0,5� of the mean fibre axis. specimens are specified in ISO 2818. Further guidance on cutting specimens is given in or on delivery), take specimens

for machining

End tabs

The ends of the specimen shall be reinforced with end tabs, preferably made of cross-ply or fabric ~lass-fibre/resin laminate with the fibres at t 45� to the specimen axis. The tab thickness shall be between 0,5 mm and 2 mm, with a tab angle of 90� (i.e. not tapered). Alternative tabbing arrangements aFe permissible, but-shall be shown, before use, to give at least equal strength and no greater coefficient of variation (see 1S0 527-1, subclause 10.5, and ISO 3534-1) than the recommended tabs. Possible alternatives include tabs made from the material under test, mechanically fastened tabs, unbended tabs made of rough materials (such as emery paper or sandpaper, and the use of roughened grip faces). If the test is carried out on untabbed specimens, tabs of made of rough tabbed specimens. 6.2.3 Application of end tabs adhesive as described in annex A. the distance between the grips shall be the same-as that between

Annex A
[normative)

Specimen preparation
A.1 Machining the specimens

In all cases take the following precautions: -- -- Avoid workhg under conditions that would create a large build-up of heat in the specimen (the use of a coolant is recommended). If a liquid coolant is used, dry the specimens immediately after machining. Check that all cut sutfaces of the specimen are free from machining defects.

A.2

Preparation

of specimens

with bonded end tabs

A recommended

method is as follows:

Cut out from the material under test a sheet having the length of the intended specimens and of a width suitable for the number of specimens required. The mean fibFe axis can be determined by splitting the edge of the test panel and examining the fibres, repeating the operation every few specimens to confirm the direction. If splitting does not give a clean edge due to misalignment between plies or layers, the panel shall not be used unless it represents a particular product or the result of a particular process. Cut out rectangular a) b) c) If required, applied. strips of the required length and width for the tabs. Attach the stripsto the sheet as follows: will be

rub with fine abrasive paper or blast with suitable sand all the surfaces to which adhesive

Remove all dust from these surfaces and clean them with a suitable solvent. Bond the strips in place along the ends of the sheet, parallel to each other and normal to the length direction of the specimens, as shown in figure A.1, using a high-stretch adhesive and strictly following the adhesive manufacturer's instructions. NOTE -- It is recommended that a film adhesive with a thin carrier be used. The adhesive should preferably have a shear strengthgreater than 30 MPa. It is desirable that the adhesive used be flexible in nature, with an elongation at break greater than that of the material under test.

d) e)

Keep the bonded pans at the pressure and temperature time recommended by the manufacturer. Cut the sheet, together with the strips constituting

recommended

by the adhesive

manufacturer

for the

the end tabs, into test specimens

(see figure A.1 ).

Annex B
(informative)

Alignment of specimens
His recommended that the alignment of the tensile-testing machine and the test specimen be checked at the centre of the gauge length using a strain-gauged coupon of the same material as is to be tested. Use a device or procedure which ensures that specimens are positioned in the grips in a repeatable manner. Strain-gauge the coupon as shown in figure B.1, attaching two gauges (SG1, SG2) to one face of the coupon approximately, oneeighth of the specimen width from the edge and midway between the tabs and attaching a third gauge (SG3) on the centreline of the opposite lace also midway between the tabs.
Compare the output of the gauges at the mid-point of the strain range used to measure Young's modulus, i.e. at 0,0015 for the strain values given in 4.6. Using equations (B.1 ) and (B.2), calculate the bending strain, expressed as a percentage, in the width (Bb) and thickness (Bh) directions, respectively. 41e2 - + 3eav lea.
